title: TCP: Handle Microsoft Large Send Offload partial checksums
description:
Microsoft Large Send Offload segmenting TCP packets larger than
the MTU uses a partial checksum calculation that uses zero for
the length field in the pseudo-header, add back in the length after
splitting as well as the payload. This is different to how Linux
handles large TCP packets.

Check for that partial checksum as well.

This could be sped up a bit by reworking the functions.

notes.body:
This reports that no TCP checksums are invalid on the capture here, either the shorter-than-MTU TCP packets where the length is used, or the larger ones where zero is used as the length:

https://ask.wireshark.org/question/36835/lots-but-not-all-of-tcp-checksum-incorrect-on-windows/

Hi @johnthacker 

There is 2 new Dead Store (and i think there is may be an issue) can you look :
```
packet-tcp.c:9044:17: warning: Value stored to 'computed_cksum' is never read [deadcode.DeadStores]
packet-tcp.c:9054:17: warning: Value stored to 'computed_cksum' is never read [deadcode.DeadStores]
```

There's no real issue, because we don't care about the return type (which isn't the full checksum), we just want the intermediate step without the last 1's complement negation. I can remove getting the return type to avoid the dead stores.
